title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #11

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Maize lives for one season and then dies. A baobab lives for many years. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Only maize is alive
   B. Plants live for different lengths of time
   C. Maize never grows
   D. Baobab does not die

2. What comes out of a bean seed first when it starts to grow? (1 mark)
   A. A root
   B. A fruit
   C. A new seed
   D. A flower

3. Which of these is a sign of life in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Being painted
   B. Feeding
   C. Being made of metal
   D. Staying in one place forever

4. What does the large intestine do with the leftovers? (1 mark)
   A. Turns them into saliva
   B. Chews them
   C. Swallows them
   D. Takes back water and forms faeces

5. What is the job of the anus? (1 mark)
   A. To make saliva
   B. To swallow food
   C. To let faeces leave the body
   D. To digest food

6. What does deworming do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes food taste better
   B. Cures a cough
   C. Kills worms in the intestines
   D. Cleans teeth

7. Which of these can be poured and takes the shape of its container? (1 mark)
   A. Stone
   B. Book
   C. Brick
   D. Water

8. Which of these is a gas? (1 mark)
   A. A wooden spoon
   B. Flour
   C. The air in a balloon
   D. Water in a cup

9. Which of these is a liquid used as fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Paraffin
   B. Air
   C. Charcoal
   D. Firewood

10. Which of these do we measure using litres? (1 mark)
   A. Length of a rope
   B. Mass of a book
   C. Volume of juice
   D. Time of a race

11. Which unit is used for the volume of milk? (1 mark)
   A. Litre
   B. Kilogram
   C. Gram
   D. Metre

12. What should never be done with waste in a place where children are playing? (1 mark)
   A. Collect it
   B. Sort it
   C. Burn it
   D. Put it in a bin

13. Which of these can be made from waste for the classroom? (1 mark)
   A. A new mountain
   B. A car engine
   C. A house
   D. A dustbin

14. Which of these is a pull? (1 mark)
   A. Closing a door by pushing
   B. Kicking a ball
   C. Pressing a bell
   D. Opening a drawer by its handle

15. Which force makes it hard to push a heavy box along a rough floor? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Light
   C. Colour
   D. Sound

16. Pulling a rope in tug of war uses (1 mark)
   A. Only gravity
   B. Only heat
   C. Only light
   D. A pull force

17. What direction does friction act in compared with the motion of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Sideways only
   B. The same
   C. Upwards only
   D. Opposite

18. What does a green traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Stop
   B. Sleep
   C. Stop at once
   D. Go

19. Why is it better to use daylight than electric light in the day? (1 mark)
   A. It costs more
   B. It saves money
   C. It makes rooms dark
   D. It is unsafe

20. Which of these is an artificial way of lighting a house? (1 mark)
   A. Electric bulbs
   B. Moonlight
   C. Windows
   D. Sun through the door

21. Why should candles and paraffin lamps be kept away from curtains? (1 mark)
   A. They make curtains cold
   B. They make curtains bright
   C. They make curtains dry
   D. They can start a fire

22. Which wall colour helps a room to be brighter? (1 mark)
   A. Dark blue
   B. Dark brown
   C. Dark black
   D. Light colours

23. Which of these is a natural source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A bulb
   B. A torch
   C. A candle
   D. The sun

24. What is the source of heat that dries fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. A jiko
   B. Electricity
   C. The sun
   D. A torch

25. Heat always moves from (1 mark)
   A. A hotter place to a cooler place
   B. A wet place to a dry place
   C. A dark place to a bright place
   D. A cooler place to a hotter place

26. In the water cycle, what does heat from the sun do? (1 mark)
   A. Removes all water
   B. Turns water into vapour
   C. Freezes water
   D. Makes water heavy

27. Which of these is a safety rule when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Turn pot handles inwards
   B. Leave children alone at the cooker
   C. Touch the hot pot
   D. Turn handles outwards

28. Why should pupils not touch hot sufurias? (1 mark)
   A. They become cold
   B. They make sound
   C. They can burn their skin
   D. They become bigger

29. Which of these passes heat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. Aluminium
   B. Copper
   C. Iron
   D. Wood

30. How does heat help plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them cold
   B. It keeps them warm enough to live
   C. It stops growth
   D. It makes them sleepy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the function of the rectum and anus. (3 marks)

32. Give three examples of things that use electricity to make heat. (3 marks)

33. Describe how to investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction using a ramp and a block. Include what you keep the same. (5 marks)

34. Draw and label a plant showing roots, stem, leaves and flower. (4 marks)

35. Describe how you can show that rough surfaces give more friction than smooth ones. (3 marks)

36. Give two safety rules when using an electric iron. (2 marks)

37. A school tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much water is lost in a school day of 8 hours and in 5 school days? (3 marks)

38. Describe five ways in which forces are used at home and on the farm. (5 marks)

39. Convert 4 kg into grams. (2 marks)

40. Make a plan for keeping your digestive system healthy for one week. (5 marks)

41. Explain how fibre helps the digestive system. (3 marks)

42. List the five groups of vertebrates and give one example of each. (3 marks)

43. Explain why a translucent roof sheet is useful in a classroom during the day. (3 marks)

44. State two dangers of leaving waste in the environment. (2 marks)

45. Explain why a kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same mass but not the same volume. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Plants live for different lengths of time
   All plants die, but some live for one season and others for many years.

2. A — A root
   The root comes out first and grows down into the soil.

3. B — Feeding
   Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die.

4. D — Takes back water and forms faeces
   Water is absorbed and the rest becomes solid waste.

5. C — To let faeces leave the body
   The anus is the opening at the end of the digestive tube.

6. C — Kills worms in the intestines
   Deworming tablets kill worms living in the intestines.

7. D — Water
   Water is a liquid.

8. C — The air in a balloon
   Air is a mixture of gases.

9. A — Paraffin
   Paraffin and petrol are liquid fuels.

10. C — Volume of juice
   Litres measure volume.

11. A — Litre
   Liquid volume is measured in millilitres and litres.

12. C — Burn it
   Burning near children is dangerous.

13. D — A dustbin
   A dustbin can be made from waste materials like a bucket or box.

14. D — Opening a drawer by its handle
   A handle is pulled toward you.

15. A — Friction
   Rough floor gives large friction.

16. D — A pull force
   Pulling is a force.

17. D — Opposite
   Friction acts against motion.

18. D — Go
   Green means go.

19. B — It saves money
   Sunlight is free.

20. A — Electric bulbs
   Bulbs are artificial light.

21. D — They can start a fire
   Flames can set cloth on fire.

22. D — Light colours
   Light colours reflect more light.

23. D — The sun
   The sun is found in nature.

24. C — The sun
   Sun heat dries fish.

25. A — A hotter place to a cooler place
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

26. B — Turns water into vapour
   Heat causes evaporation from seas and rivers.

27. A — Turn pot handles inwards
   Handles turned inwards cannot be knocked easily.

28. C — They can burn their skin
   Hot metal burns.

29. D — Wood
   Wood is a poor passer of heat.

30. B — It keeps them warm enough to live
   Life needs suitable warmth.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: The rectum stores faeces for a short time and the anus is the opening through which faeces leave the body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rectum, 1 mark for anus, 1 mark for describing waste leaving.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric kettle, iron, cooker, heater, hair dryer, toaster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a ramp. Slide a block down it covered with cloth, paper, cardboard and bare board. Measure how far it slides each time. Keep the same block, same ramp height and same push. Record in a table. The shortest distance shows the most friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for ramp, 1 mark for surfaces, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for fair test, 1 mark for conclusion.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with four correctly labelled parts: roots below the ground, stem upright, leaves on the stem and a flower at the top.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correctly drawn and labelled part.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Slide the same block down a ramp covered with different surfaces. It travels a shorter distance on rough surfaces than on smooth ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch it while hot, switch off after use, keep it away from children, do not touch with wet hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 16 litres in one day and 80 litres in five days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 x 8, 1 mark for 16, 1 mark for 16 x 5 = 80.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Pushing a wheelbarrow, pulling a plough, lifting water from a well with a rope, hammering a nail, kicking a ball, stitching clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4000 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan including brushing teeth twice a day, eating fruits and vegetables, drinking clean water, washing hands, chewing well, deworming as advised and limiting sweets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible action up to 5.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fibre in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food and waste move through the intestines and helps prevent constipation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming fibre foods, 1 mark for movement, 1 mark for constipation.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mammals (goat), birds (hen), reptiles (snake), amphibians (frog), fish (tilapia).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct five groups, 1 mark for four examples, 1 mark for correct matching.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: It lets daylight in, so lamps are not needed, saving electricity and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for daylight, 1 mark for no lamps, 1 mark for saving.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Blocked drains and floods, disease from flies and rats, harm to animals, injuries from glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each danger.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both have 1 kg of matter. The feathers take up more space than the stones so their volume is larger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equal mass, 1 mark for the meaning of mass, 1 mark for feathers taking more space, 1 mark for volume being space.
